title: Annotatio IV §.III (3): Mode compatible with ascension — Athanasius draws from corporal intellect
pass_a_gloss: (3) Because that presence with participation of Christ’s body and blood alone is commended which also rightly consists with the ascent of Christ’s body into heaven — nay, from the ascent into Heaven against disciples who, while He was still present on earth, interposed and struggled against eating His flesh and blood, could be proved by these words of Christ: What then if you should see the Son of Man ascending where He was before? (v. 62). But not Corporal presence on earth from the ascent of Christ’s body into Heaven, but Spiritual only, was ready to be gathered and demonstrated. Therefore He mentions His ascension, says Athanasius — that He might draw them away from corporal intellect and that thereafter they might learn His flesh to be heavenly and spiritual food.
pass_b_english: (3) The recommended presence must also stand with Christ’s bodily ascent into heaven (John 6:62) — so from the ascent one gathers spiritual presence on earth, not corporal.
Athanasius: He named the ascension to pull them off corporal intellect and teach His flesh as heavenly spiritual food. (Greek transliterated in Pass B.)
source_text: (3) Quia ista solummodò præsentia cum participatione corporis & sanguinis Christi commendatur, quæ etiam cum adscensu corporis Christi in cælum, probè consistere, quin ex adscensu corporis Christi in Cœlum, contra discipulos, manducationi carnis ejus & sanguinis, dum coram adhuc adesset, in terris intercedentes ac obluctati, evinci hisce Christi verbis poterat: Quid si igitur spectaveritis Filium Hominis adscendentem eo, ubi erat priùs? vers. 62. At non Corporalis in terris præsentia ex adscensu corporis Christi in Cœlum, sed Spiritualis tantùm, colligi demonstrarique in promptu erat. Proptereà adscensionis suæ meminit, inquit Athanasius: hina somatikēs ennoias autous aphelkysēi — eos, à corporali intellectu abstraheret & ut deinceps carnem suam cœlestem & spiritualem cibum esse discerent, Tom. I. tract. in illud: Qui dixerit verbum contra Spir. S.
